title: If the rent covers the instalment, is it a good investment?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #251 | DEFINITION OF A GOOD INVESTMENT PROJECT
excerpt: A 24-year-old whose first subsale rented out in four days asks whether rent covering the instalment makes a good deal, and whether to buy a completed unsold unit next.

qa.asker: Flash, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: Flash is 24 and works in healthcare. He bought a subsale unit in his hometown, fully furnished it and rented it out within four days, with the rent covering the instalment and maintenance. He is now looking at a completed project in i-City, Shah Alam, where the developer still has unsold units with zero down payment and about RM30,000 cash back, and where the rent would also cover the instalment.
qa.question: Is a property a good investment as long as the rent covers the instalment, is he moving too fast on a second unit, and does a completed project with unsold units mean it is a bad property?
qa.quote: As long as a rent can cover installment, I'm good.
qa.answer: At his stage, yes: if the rent covers the instalment and maintenance, the tenant pays off a property he will own outright in about 30 years, even with no price growth. A completed project with unsold units can be the best of both worlds, provided he checks subsale prices and can carry both units empty for six months.

reasons.title: The flipping era is over
reasons.body: When Sean started there were developer interest-bearing schemes, no two-loan limit on 90% financing and easy loan approvals, so buyers flipped new launches. Now developers price that gain in, so he plays the equity game: hold units whose rent covers the instalment.

reasons.title: Strategy depends on your money
reasons.body: Someone with RM5 million in cash compares property with fixed deposits and the S&P 500 and may buy corner-lot landed homes, shop lots or land for capital growth. Rent covering the instalment is the strategy for people who rely on bank financing.

reasons.title: Completed unsold units remove the guesswork
reasons.body: You can see the orientation, build quality, facilities, existing rents and resident complaints, while still getting developer incentives. Compare with subsale prices for the same size: a cheaper subsale needs about 18% upfront but gives better cash flow.

reasons.title: Unsold usually means overpriced, not bad
reasons.body: Developers, especially listed ones, often set ambitious prices. Oversupply helps investors because struggling developers offer deals; when everyone is rushing to buy, Sean thinks it is time to stop.

actions: Start in an area you know well, where you understand traffic, schools and local habits.
Fully furnish a rental unit so it lets quickly.
Check that a unit has more than one rental option: long-term, room by room, short stay, or per head near students and hospitals.
Compare the developer's price with recent subsale transactions of the same size before buying.
Before a second unit, make sure your job is secure and you can carry both units empty for six months.
qa.caveat: This is the cash-flow strategy for buyers relying on loans. Sean expects his own strategy to change as his portfolio grows, towards landed, commercial or industrial property with more risk and more capital.
